title: Primary structure that stores the host system’s useful energy

concept.text: The innovation is a primary load-bearing structure that also stores and supplies the electrical energy needed for its host system’s useful mission. A vehicle chassis member or aircraft structural element would serve simultaneously as part of the load path and as an energy-storage device. Structural batteries provide the material basis for this idea by combining mechanical load bearing with electrochemical storage.

Scope synthesis: the defining advance would be demonstrated integration at the level of a working system. The structure must carry its declared loads and deliver useful mission energy while meeting requirements for aging, damage tolerance and safety. Installing conventional batteries inside a structural enclosure, or demonstrating energy storage and stiffness in a material specimen, would not by itself establish this capability. The supplied evidence establishes multifunctional material performance, but does not establish this mission-serving primary structure.

significance.text: Combining energy storage with primary structure could change how vehicles, aircraft and portable systems allocate mass. Material already needed to support loads could also contribute stored energy, reducing the requirement for separate batteries and making structural geometry, material selection and energy capacity parts of the same design problem. The 2024 paper identifies replacing structural vehicle parts while reducing conventional batteries as an intended application; this supports the integration opportunity, rather than proving complete mission-battery replacement.

System-level inference: a substantial net mass saving would be revolutionary for machines whose payload, range or endurance is constrained by mass, but its magnitude cannot be inferred from eliminating a separate pack alone. Usable energy, structural efficiency, electrical connections, protective systems, inspection access and repair provisions all enter the mass budget. A structural battery with lower energy per kilogram could still be advantageous if it replaces enough otherwise necessary structural mass; conversely, integration overhead could consume the benefit. A comparison against an equivalent conventional structure and battery system is therefore essential.

Application-boundary synthesis: ambient-energy harvesting is a separate capability because it generates energy from the environment, whereas this concept stores previously supplied energy. No numerical harvesting-power comparison is established here. Extending structural storage to occupied building frames or city-scale grid storage would require additional materials, fire-safety, durability and repair demonstrations. Results in carbon-fiber vehicle materials would not establish the suitability of ordinary building materials or the safety of embedding battery chemistry throughout occupied primary structure.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability in the supplied evidence is a primary member that supplies a declared useful mission’s energy and retains acceptable structural performance after electrochemical aging and relevant mechanical damage. The retained sources demonstrate the dual-function material concept and describe continuing investigation of mechanical and electrochemical interactions. They do not establish mission-scale qualification. This is an evidence boundary, not a finding that no later qualifying demonstration exists.

Engineering synthesis: the material must provide adequate usable energy and power while preserving stiffness, strength and load transfer. These functions must remain compatible during charging, discharging, repeated loading and environmental exposure. The central question is not simply whether both functions exist initially, but whether their interaction leaves sufficient margins over the intended service life. High initial longitudinal modulus and efficient charge transfer alone do not answer that question.

Engineering synthesis: scaling introduces joints, electrical connections, insulation, manufacturing variability, inspection and repair requirements. Impact or penetration can affect both the load path and the electrical system, so damage containment and residual structural capacity must be assessed together. Thermal events also require application-specific protection and a defined safe structural response. These are concrete qualification questions; the supplied retained evidence does not quantify their severity or establish their solutions.

The earlier research attributes a broader barrier list to the November 2025 review: low energy density, competing electrochemical and mechanical requirements, cost, fatigue and impact sensitivity, volume change, and a lack of standard tests. That publication has no retained text in the supplied evidence review. The list remains an attributed account requiring verification, rather than an inspected finding or proof that no applicable test methods exist.

current_state.text: Richa Chaudhary, Johanna Xu, Zhenyuan Xia and Leif E. Asp reported an all-carbon-fiber structural battery composite in “Unveiling the Multifunctional Carbon Fiber Structural Battery,” published online on 10 September 2024. The retained PubMed abstract reports energy density of 30 Wh/kg, cyclic stability up to 1000 cycles with approximately 100 percent coulombic efficiency, and elastic modulus above 76 GPa parallel to the fibers. These are reported material-level results. The retained evidence is an abstract, not the full research article, and does not establish specimen dimensions, mission-scale integration or structural certification.

Coulombic efficiency describes the relationship between charge delivered and charge supplied during cycling; it does not, by itself, establish retained energy capacity or mechanical durability. Likewise, the reported modulus is directional: performance parallel to the fibers cannot be treated as a complete description of structural behavior under other loading directions or damage conditions. The retained abstract does not provide the tensile-strength and post-cycling mechanical measurements asserted in the earlier account.

The earlier research attributes pristine tensile strength as high as about 790 MPa and post-cycling values of about 65 GPa modulus and 612 MPa strength in one configuration to Asp and Chaudhary’s “All-carbon fibre structural battery composites,” dated 23 February 2025. Its citation points to DOI 10.1177/1045389X251320443, but no source text was retained for the validated review. These numerical assertions remain unverified within this record and cannot establish a measured degradation trend without their test conditions, specimen correspondence and cycling history. Missing source text is not evidence that the values are false.

A retained Chalmers institutional article reports an ongoing study with energy density above 60 Wh/kg and elastic modulus above 100 GPa. The page was published on 24 June 2025 and updated on 27 January 2026, so its retained version cannot establish when each performance statement first appeared. These figures are verified as institutional statements about ongoing work; the underlying measurements and research paper were not inspected in the supplied review. They should not be presented as independently validated performance or a completed mission-scale demonstration.

Evidence-boundary synthesis: the supplied record contains no bounded freshness search establishing the field’s completeness through 1 November 2026. It therefore cannot determine whether a later mission-scale demonstration or a paper supporting the higher Chalmers figures had appeared by that date. The earlier comparison against contemporary lithium-ion packs exceeding 150 Wh/kg also lacks retained supporting evidence and is not used as a quantitative benchmark. These limitations leave the dated 2024 results intact.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: build a vehicle- or aircraft-scale primary element, or a complete small-vehicle chassis, that carries declared design loads and supplies the electrical energy required for a declared useful mission without a separate mission-energy pack. Specify mission duration, operating conditions, usable energy, required power, structural allowables and acceptance thresholds before testing. A material specimen reporting 30 Wh/kg and 76 GPa alone would not satisfy this proposed system-level criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and damage demonstration: repeat the structural and mission-energy assessments after a declared number of charge cycles and an application-relevant mechanical load history. Measure capacity retention and mechanical performance separately, and evaluate their interaction under representative operating conditions. Impact, penetration and fire tests should declare exposure conditions and required residual structural capacity, including the period over which that capacity must be maintained. These are proposed assessment criteria, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed durability and damage demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical validation: report material composition, manufacturing methods, specimen geometry, interfaces, test procedures and variation across multiple builds. Independent reproduction should confirm both energy delivery and structural performance. A system comparison should include protection, connections, inspection and repair provisions, and should quantify any mass saving against an equivalent conventional structure and battery system.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical validation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed boundary statement: define the demonstrated operating envelope, including temperature, loading directions, service duration, allowable damage and repair assumptions. Finite testing can establish performance across that declared envelope; it cannot establish universal durability or safety under every mission and damage scenario. Qualification would remain specific to the intended application and its applicable requirements.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed boundary statement

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: STR-01, “Flaw-tolerant bulk members at near-theoretical specific strength,” concerns structural performance despite flaws. It overlaps STR-08 where damage tolerance affects safe energy-bearing members, but exceptional specific strength does not establish useful energy storage. STR-02, “Repeated autonomous restoration of full structural capacity,” addresses recovery after damage. Combining it with STR-08 would additionally require restoration or safe isolation of damaged electrochemical functions; neither capability implies the other.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-03, “A cast mineral solid that can be a complete primary structure,” shares the goal of extending a material’s structural role, but concerns a different material system and does not imply electrochemical storage. STR-05, “Primary members whose mechanical state can be reprogrammed in service,” and STR-06, “Load-bearing structures that grow and remodel,” concern changes to mechanical behavior or structural form. STR-08 could potentially supply energy for such functions, but storage alone establishes neither reprogramming nor growth.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-04, “Field-scale broadband seismic cloaking,” STR-10, “Ordinary buildings that remain undamaged and usable after design-level earthquakes,” and STR-11, “Passive damping that removes resonant amplification from governing modes,” address structural response to excitation or earthquake damage. Their overlap with STR-08 is the need to preserve load-bearing performance under relevant dynamic conditions. Energy storage does not itself provide seismic cloaking, prevent earthquake damage or establish passive damping.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-07, “Topological control that denies an undesigned collapse mechanism,” and STR-12, “Disproportionate collapse made unavailable after loss of any one primary member,” address system-level collapse behavior. They become relevant when damage to an energy-storing primary member could compromise the load path. STR-08 would need an appropriate structural safety strategy, but multifunctional material performance does not establish either collapse-control capability.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-09, “A prospectively validated law of structural lifespan,” overlaps directly with the need to understand coupled electrochemical aging and structural service life. STR-08 requires credible durability evidence for its declared application; it does not require, or establish, a general predictive law of structural lifespan. The concepts remain distinct even if lifespan prediction would make structural batteries easier to design and maintain.

change_log.change: Preserved STR-08’s identity and centered its explanation on primary structure supplying useful mission energy.
change_log.reason: The concept extends beyond a material that separately exhibits stiffness and energy storage, and the supplied review does not establish its system-level achievement.

change_log.change: Replaced the universal description of batteries as parasitic mass and the promise of a large mass reduction with a conditional system-level benefit.
change_log.reason: Net savings depend on structural efficiency, usable energy and integration overhead; no complete comparative mass budget is supplied.

change_log.change: Retained the supported 2024 energy density, cycle count, coulombic efficiency and longitudinal modulus with their date and abstract-only access limitation.
change_log.reason: These results are supported within their reported scope and should survive corrections to other assertions.

change_log.change: Separated coulombic efficiency from capacity retention and mechanical durability, and emphasized the directional scope of the modulus.
change_log.reason: The reported metrics do not establish retained mission energy, complete structural behavior or post-aging allowables.

change_log.change: Preserved the 790 MPa, 65 GPa and 612 MPa assertions as explicitly unverified attributions.
change_log.reason: The user requested preservation of unresolved quantitative detail; the missing Sage source text prevents treating these values or a degradation trend as verified.

change_log.change: Corrected the chronology and evidentiary status of the Chalmers figures above 60 Wh/kg and 100 GPa.
change_log.reason: The retained institutional page was updated in January 2026, and no underlying measurement paper was inspected.

change_log.change: Removed the unsupported contemporary pack benchmark from the technical comparison and qualified claims about small-cell scope and absence of later demonstrations.
change_log.reason: The retained evidence does not establish those comparisons, specimen dimensions or field completeness through November 2026.

change_log.change: Retained the November 2025 review’s attributed barrier list while distinguishing it from engineering synthesis.
change_log.reason: The publication has no retained text, so its exact findings and authorship cannot be verified from the supplied review.

change_log.change: Expanded completion proposals to declare missions, loads, aging histories, damage exposures, acceptance thresholds, reproducibility and practical integration boundaries.
change_log.reason: These details make a future demonstration assessable without implying consensus standards or universal performance.

change_log.change: Integrated distinctions involving ambient harvesting, occupied-building storage and all other supplied roster entries.
change_log.reason: These connections clarify relevant overlap without merging independent innovations or extrapolating vehicle-material results to buildings.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether a qualifying mission-serving primary structure had been demonstrated by 1 November 2026.

The underlying study, measurement conditions and publication status supporting Chalmers’ figures above 60 Wh/kg and 100 GPa remain unverified; the date those statements first appeared is also unresolved.

The Sage article’s reported strength and post-cycling values require source verification, including specimen correspondence, loading direction and cycling conditions. The review’s recommendation to remove these numbers entirely was not adopted because the user explicitly requested preservation of unresolved quantitative detail; they are retained only as unverified attributions.
The November 2025 review’s exact barrier discussion and authorship remain unverified because no text was retained.
Capacity retention, post-aging structural allowables, combined damage-and-cycling behavior, specimen dimensions and certification status cannot be established from the retained 2024 abstract.
No supported system-level comparison establishes net mass savings or a contemporary conventional-pack energy-density benchmark.
The proposed completion criteria still require application-specific numerical thresholds and qualification requirements before they can become an executable demonstration program.
